solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cattle going round English port

indicators.note: going round says the cattle word encircles the next piece

parts.note: cows are cattle

explanation.surface: A herd of cattle being driven around a seaside town in England.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Wight town is a harbour famous for its yachting regatta, hence a port.

clue.text: In mixed school pupil initially got by

indicators.note: In says the pupil's letter goes inside the school word

parts.note: a co-ed school takes both boys and girls

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word pupil

explanation.surface: A pupil at a co-educational school manages to scrape through.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is to manage or survive adequately, a close synonym of handling a difficulty.

clue.text: Café employee with a sister in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of a sister are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A café worker whose sister has got herself into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles A SISTER into AITRESS, placed after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves tables in a café is a server employed there.

clue.text: Perfume put in the post, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a letter put in the post has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a bottle of perfume was mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a pleasant fragrance, the usual synonym for a perfume.

clue.text: The art of comedy? There's something fishy here

definitions.meaning: comedy is the trade of being amusing, so a playful reading of the phrase
something suspicious or underhand going on

explanation.surface: A comic's craft set against a hint of dodgy dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally, as the trade of being amusing; the question mark flags that whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shady or deceitful activity, and literally a trade in jokes.

clue.text: Dog that is trailing Antarctic explorer

indicators.note: trailing says the that-is letters follow behind the explorer

parts.note: Captain Robert Falcon Scott led the ill-fated South Pole expedition
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sled dog following behind a polar explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish terrier is a breed, so a specific example of a canine.

clue.text: Learner doctor bandages one leg, perhaps

indicators.note: bandages says the doctor wraps around the next piece

parts.note: L is a learner, from British L-plates on learner drivers' cars
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trainee medic dressing a patient's injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The learner and the doctor together, L and MB, wrap around I.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is an appendage of the body; 'perhaps' marks a leg as one example.

clue.text: Spy resting in overnight carriage

definitions.meaning: an agent planted long in advance who lies dormant until activated
a railway coach with berths for travelling through the night

explanation.surface: A secret agent dozing on a night train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resting in' joins the two senses and pays out a third hint: someone resting is asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a dormant agent, and a train car fitted with bunks.

clue.text: Wartime leader unwell after Sunday service?

indicators.note: after places the unwell word behind the service word

parts.note: going to church is the Sunday service
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A leader feeling poorly after attending worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston led Britain as Prime Minister through the Second World War.

clue.text: Force smallest possible wage increase?

parts.note: P, a penny, is the smallest British coin, so the least amount
a rise is a British pay increase

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a worker should push for the tiniest pay bump.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny rise is the smallest possible raise; 'Force' looks like a verb about pressuring the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something is to lever it open by force.

clue.text: Famous person without talent

definitions.meaning: read as two words, lacking ability

explanation.surface: A celebrity who has no real gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a prominent figure; split in two it says incapable.

clue.text: Door repaired by your old woman

indicators.note: repaired means the door is put back together in a new order

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A wife who had the door fixed for her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so this stands for one woman.

clue.text: Platoon ordered to carry equipment

indicators.note: to carry has the commanded word holding the gear word within

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, so ordered
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Soldiers commanded to take their kit with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the anagram signal for Platoon, but it is BADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are army units; the setter uses one formation loosely for another.

clue.text: Horny creature and social worker run off together

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a social insect colony
lovers who elope run away to marry

explanation.surface: A randy animal and a caseworker running off as a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: This African grazing mammal carries horns, hence a horned beast.

clue.text: Western assassin who was a poet

parts.note: a hitman is a hired killer

explanation.surface: A cowboy-film gunman who wrote verse on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt, author of Leaves of Grass, is a celebrated American writer of verse.

clue.text: Heard of my fantastic move abroad

indicators.note: Heard signals that a spoken phrase gives the letters

parts.note: my gives MY; fantastic means great

explanation.surface: Hearing of a wonderful plan to emigrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate to another country or region is the verb for travelling to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Self-important person, and what he needs when using pens?

definitions.meaning: a pompous figure, mockingly given a mock title

definitions.text: what he needs when using pens?
definitions.meaning: a male writer's pen points belong to him

explanation.surface: A pompous man fussing over his writing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Old dip pens took detachable metal points, so a man writing with them needs his own.
explanation.definitionFit: The jocular title mocks a pompous man; literally it names a man's pen points.

clue.text: Type of lettuce that's reduced in very warm weather?

definitions.text: that's reduced in very warm weather?
definitions.meaning: a floating mass of frozen water melts and shrinks in heat

explanation.surface: A salad leaf that wilts in a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a crisp salad variety and a floating ice mass that melts in warmth.

clue.text: One with small part in film run?

definitions.text: One with small part in film
definitions.meaning: a background actor in a crowd scene
in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor in a movie's run in cinemas.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs credited to the batting side but not hit off the bat are extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit-part player and a bonus cricket score share the same name.

clue.text: Implied farm animal can carry tons

indicators.note: can carry has the animal holding the tons letter within

parts.note: a goat is a farmyard beast

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a farm beast can haul heavy loads.
explanation.definitionFit: What someone is getting at is what they hint at, so the past form means hinted.

clue.text: Capital city rebuilt there, near Afghanistan's borders

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of there are put back together in another order
borders takes the edge letters of the word Afghanistan's

explanation.surface: A capital reconstructed near the Afghan frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns THERE into TEHER; the borders of AFGHANISTAN (ignoring the apostrophe) are A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older spelling of the capital of Iran, Afghanistan's western neighbour.

clue.text: Beer ingredients used by teashop sometimes

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tearoom that occasionally brews its own beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried flowers of the climbing plant give bitterness and aroma to brewed ale.

clue.text: Fish starters in top restaurant no longer fashionable

indicators.note: starters picks the opening letters of top and restaurant

parts.note: out means out of fashion

explanation.surface: A fish starter in a smart restaurant that has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like the menu course, but it picks first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Early dish, mixture of tripe and peas

indicators.note: a mixture blends tripe and peas into a new order

explanation.surface: A first course of tripe mixed with peas.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter served at the beginning of a meal, so it comes early.

clue.text: Representative, a courteous fellow

parts.note: a gent is short for gentleman, a polite man

explanation.surface: A sales rep who is a polite chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts on another's behalf, such as a sales or literary rep.
